texts: One day before the autumn equinox of Year 1, Bevin Coombe walked the Cove Stair at sundown.
Bevin Coombe touched the iron bands of the Stilllight Lantern.
Bevin Coombe lit the Stilllight Lantern.
The Stilllight Lantern burned mire-essence through the night.
Bevin Coombe walked the Cove Stair again at midnight.
Bevin Coombe walked the Cove Stair again at the third watch.
Bevin Coombe refreshed the mire-essence of the Stilllight Lantern at midnight.
Bevin Coombe trimmed the wick of the Stilllight Lantern at the third watch.

q2_gaps: a durative 'through the <day-part>' frame adverbial ('burned mire-essence through the night') has no licensed carrier: `During` is restricted to during/while/throughout and may not take a synonym head, `(Measure e duration n u)` needs a stated count+unit, and Start/End need stated terms, so the throughout-ness is lost in the plain `(Time e night)`

an event-noun used as a temporal anchor is told to get 'its class atom and the ordering relation and nothing else', but the instruction set does not say what to do with a calendar restrictor stated inside that anchor NP ('the autumn equinox **of Year 1**') — dropping it would silently drop a stated qualifier
review.notes: Roles, tense, `Again` tags, the `BeforeBy` measured gap, the name/kind split on Cove Stair and Stilllight Lantern, and the compound genus atoms (autumn_equinox, iron_band, mire_essence) all follow the instruction set; the of-phrase split between PartOf (bands, wick) and Possession (mire-essence) is a defensible reading of the part/component test. 'Walked the Cove Stair' takes Theme via the explicit unclear-case default; `mire_essence` is a bare kind filler in sentence 4 but a witness `sk_essence_1` in sentence 7, so the two mentions do not corefer.
